purpose: Record source statements and code mappings relevant to the Mukunda-Paul and Ma erosive burn-rate closures. This is not a complete T02 record and does not establish model validation or applicability to any coupled run.

sources.citation: H. S. Mukunda and P. J. Paul, 'Universal Behaviour in Erosive Burning of Solid Propellants,' Combustion and Flame 109 (1997), 224-236. Local source: docs/references/mukunda1997.pdf.

anchors.content: The authors define the normalized enhancement as actual/nonerosive burn rate and describe g0 as free-stream mass flux divided by nonerosive surface mass flux; Re0 is based on nonerosive mass flux and port diameter. The abstract reports m=-0.125 and says most compiled data correlate within experimental accuracy.

anchors.location: printed p. 226, Eqs. (9)-(11) and accompanying text
anchors.content: The source defines g = g0 (Re0/1000)^m, with m selected as -0.125. Re0 is based on nonerosive mass burn rate and port diameter. Eq. (10) gives an enhancement of the form eta = 1 + K1 (g^0.8 - g_th^0.8) H(g-g_th); the text states K1 and g_th are determined from data and K2 is only a scaling choice.

anchors.location: printed p. 234, Eq. (12) and concluding remarks
anchors.content: The recommended fitted universal expression is eta = 1 + 0.023 (g^0.8 - g_th^0.8) H(g-g_th), where g = g0 (Re0/1000)^(-0.125), g_th = 35.0. The authors describe the fit as within approximately +/-10% of the data for most practical propellants, while explicitly noting unresolved negative-erosion behavior.

anchors.location: printed pp. 233-234, data summary and Eq. (12) discussion
anchors.content: The paper reports 390 discrete points in the assembled data plot, with roughly 60 additional points imputed for two data sets whose counts were unclear; 373 points fall within the stated +/-15% band and 77 outside. These are the paper's reported compilation/fit statistics, not an independent validation of this code.

definitions_and_units.G: port gas mass flux [kg m^-2 s^-1]
definitions_and_units.d0: port characteristic diameter [m] (hydraulic diameter for most sources in the paper)

code_mapping.mapping: The implementation computes g0, Re0, g, threshold 35, exponent 0.8 and coefficient 0.023 as in Eq. (12), then returns total rate r0*eta. The caller reconstructs G as Re_local*dynamic_viscosity/D_hyd and supplies D_hyd as d0. This is an algebraic mapping of the code inputs, not evidence that the coupled solver's local values satisfy the source's experimental assumptions.

sources.evidence_class: published correlation and authors' reported compiled-data fit; no local-run validation

sources.citation: Y. Ma, F. Bao, L. Sun, Y. Liu, and W. Hui, 'A New Erosive Burning Model of Solid Propellant Based on Heat Transfer Equilibrium at Propellant Surface,' International Journal of Aerospace Engineering (2020), Article 8889333, doi:10.1155/2020/8889333. Local source: docs/references/International Journal of Aerospace Engineering - 2020 - Ma - A New Erosive Burning Model of Solid Propellant Based on Heat.pdf.

anchors.content: The paper writes r=r0+re, r0=a P^n, assumes re=k Q, balances Q=re rho_p Cps (Ts-Ti), obtains k=1/[rho_p Cps (Ts-Ti)], and then gives r=a P^n + [(T_infinity-Ts)/(rho_p Cps (Ts-Ti))] h. It identifies Q=h(T_infinity-Ts). The paper says reaction heat release at the surface is ignored in this balance.

The source specifies laminar, turbulent, and transitional Nusselt treatments (Eqs. 8-10), Nu=h0 D/lambda (Eq. 11), roughness-dependent Darcy friction (including Haaland Eq. 15), and transpiration correction h/h0=beta_th/[exp(beta_th)-1] (Eq. 16), with beta_th=rho_p r Cp/h0 after assuming rho v_g=rho_p r.

anchors.location: printed pp. 3 and 5-8, Table 1 and Sec. 3
anchors.content: The article tabulates example composite formulations and properties (Table 1, p. 3), compares calculations against selected published propellant and motor cases, and describes using CEA for some gas transport properties. The abstract reports about 10% agreement for the comparisons presented. This is coverage of those source cases only; it does not document the input provenance or validity of the local coupled motor cases considered here.

formula_and_units.total_rate: r = r0 + ((T_infinity - Ts) / (rho_p * Cps * (Ts - Ti))) * h
formula_and_units.heat_transfer: h = h0 * beta/(exp(beta)-1); beta = rho_p * r * Cp_gas / h0
formula_and_units.rho_p_Cps_T: rho_p [kg m^-3], Cps [J kg^-1 K^-1], temperatures [K]
formula_and_units.Nu_Pr_Re_beta: dimensionless; lambda [W m^-1 K^-1]; D and L [m]

code_mapping.mapping: burn_rate_cell obtains r0 from the tabulated Saint-Robert law; computes f, Nu, and h0; forms ebf=(T_flame-T_surface)/(rho_p*Cps*(T_surface-T_initial)); forms alpha=rho_p*Cp_gas/h0 so beta=alpha*r; and solves r-r0-ebf*h0*beta/(exp(beta)-1)=0 by bisection. This matches the algebraic structure of Ma Eqs. 2-7 and 16. The heat-transfer path implements the cited Ma correlation family at Eqs. 8-15, subject to local implementation choices documented in code.

ma_eq_8_laminar_nusselt.note: Code adds 0.7^3 term and max(Nu2-0.7,0) guard from Gnielinski 2013 Eq. 8 composite formulation; Ma Eq. 8 is a simplified presentation

ma_eq_9_turbulent_nusselt.code: f8=f/8; num=f8*(Re-1000)*Pr; den=1+12.7*sqrt(f8)*(Pr**(2/3)-1); entrance=1+(D/L)**(2/3); K=(T_gas/T_surface)^kappa; Nu_turb=max(num/den,0)*entrance*K
ma_eq_9_turbulent_nusselt.note: Direct transcription of modified Petukhov-Kirillov with Gnielinski correction; Re-1000 cutoff matches source

ma_eq_10_transition_nusselt.note: Linear blend in Re=[2300,4000]; clamping matches code guard

ma_eq_15_haaland_friction.source: 1/sqrt(f) = -1.8*log10((eps/D)^1.11/3.7^1.11 + 6.9/Re) for turbulent; f=64/Re for laminar; linear blend in transition
ma_eq_15_haaland_friction.code: inv_sqrt_f = -1.8*log10(eps_rel**1.11/3.7**1.11 + 6.9/Re); f_turb=1/inv_sqrt_f^2; f_lam=64/Re; linear blend gamma=(Re-2300)/1700
ma_eq_15_haaland_friction.note: Exact transcription of Haaland 1983 with Re>=2300/4000 regime split; 1.11 exponent matches source

ma_eq_16_transpiration.source: h/h0 = beta/(exp(beta)-1); beta = rho_p * r * Cp / h0
ma_eq_16_transpiration.code: beta = alpha * r where alpha = rho_p * Cp_gas / h0; transpiration_correction returns beta/(exp(beta)-1) with small-beta Taylor and clamp [0,1]
ma_eq_16_transpiration.note: beta_th = beta in code; small-beta expansion 1-beta/2 avoids 0/0; clamp prevents numerical overflow

ma_eqs_2_7_energy_balance.source: r = r0 + ((T_inf - Ts)/(rho_p*Cps*(Ts-Ti))) * h; r0 = a*P^n
ma_eqs_2_7_energy_balance.code: r0 = saint_robert_from_tabs(P); ebf = (T_flame-T_surface)/(rho_p*Cps*(T_surface-T_initial)); solves r = r0 + ebf * h0 * beta/(exp(beta)-1) by bisection
ma_eqs_2_7_energy_balance.note: T_infinity mapped to T_flame; implicit coupling via beta(r) solved by monotone bisection

unresolved_for_actual_coupled_input_appl: The local PDFs do not establish that the material-specific a, n, rho_p, Cps, Ti, Ts, T_flame, Cp_gas, Pr, conductivity, viscosity, roughness, or pressure ranges supplied to any current coupled run match the source case definitions or have traceable measurements for that propellant.

For Mukunda-Paul, applicability depends on local G, r0, hydraulic/characteristic diameter, and viscosity; source coverage does not independently verify the solver's reconstructed local G or choice of D_hyd as the source characteristic length for each geometry or transient state.

For Ma, the heat balance neglects surface reaction heat and the paper's use of constant wall temperature, convection-dominant transfer, property treatment, entrance length, and transpiration assumptions need case-by-case checks against the actual flow and material inputs.

No coupled-run input snapshot, code-path fingerprint, independent experimental measurement comparison, or uncertainty propagation is included here. Numerical agreement or convergence is not evidence that these source assumptions apply.

ma_closure.summary: The Ma closure equations (Eqs. 2-16) are fully transcribed in code per the equation audit above. However, the following source assumptions require case-by-case verification against actual coupled-run inputs:

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Constant wall temperature (T_surface) and convection-dominant heat transfer
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses fixed T_surface and T_flame from propellant table. No surface energy balance or ablation model. Real surface temperature varies with pressure, erosion, and time.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Gas properties (Pr, Cp_gas, lambda, mu) evaluated at film temperature or bulk gas temperature
assumptions_needing_verification.source_loc: Ma Sec. 2.1-2.3; Table 1 uses CEA-derived properties
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code accepts scalar Pr, Cp_gas, k_thermal, mu from caller. In Chunc runs: Pr=0.45, Cp_gas=2000, k_thermal=0.15, mu=6.5e-5 (constants). Source uses temperature-dependent properties from CEA. Constant-property approximation may misrepresent heat transfer at high temperature gradients.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Entrance length L = distance from head end (x_from_head)
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses x_from_head as L. For Chunc (L/D ~ 5-10), entrance region is significant. For segmented grains, 'head end' definition is ambiguous. No virtual origin or developed-flow correction.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Hydraulic diameter D as characteristic length for both friction and heat transfer
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses D_hyd from geometry. For non-circular ports, D_hyd = 4*A/P. Source developed for circular pipes; equivalence not established for slotted/star grains.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Roughness epsilon = 35 microns (Chunc) is physically representative of burning surface
assumptions_needing_verification.source_loc: Haaland correlation (Ma Eq. 15); Table 1 uses 10-50 um range
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses constant roughness. Real roughness evolves with burn-back, aluminized vs non-aluminized propellant, and pressure. Chunc value 35 um is within source range but not measured for this propellant.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Transpiration model assumes rho*v_g = rho_p*r (steady 1D mass flux at surface)
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses this directly. Valid for quasi-steady port flow; may not hold during startup transients with rapid pressure changes.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Neglect of surface reaction heat release in energy balance
assumptions_needing_verification.source_loc: Ma Eq. 2-7 text: 'reaction heat release at the surface is ignored'
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code does not include surface reaction term. For composite propellants with surface reactions (e.g., AP decomposition), this omits a heat source that could affect T_surface and heat transfer.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Gnielinski kappa = 0.45 for gas heating (T_gas > T_wall)
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses kappa=0.45 default. Chunc runs use 0.45. Valid for T_gas > T_wall which holds in motors. Not verified for all propellant combinations.

mukunda_paul_closure.summary: The Mukunda-Paul Eq. 12 is fully transcribed. Applicability assumptions:

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Nonerosive burn rate r0 from Saint-Robert law at local pressure
assumptions_needing_verification.source_loc: Eq. 12 derivation: Re0 = rho_p * r0 * d0 / mu
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses tabulated a, n at cell pressure. Valid if r0 is well-characterized. For Chunc, r0 from same propellant table as Ma.

assumptions_needing_verification.source_loc: Paper uses 'port diameter' for most sources
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Code uses D_hyd. For non-circular ports, this is an assumption. Paper's data compilation used mostly circular ports.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Mass flux G reconstructed from Re_local * mu / D_hyd
assumptions_needing_verification.source_loc: Code mapping; paper uses free-stream mass flux
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Re_local is from solver's quasi-1D flow. G reconstruction assumes 1D uniformity. Startup transients may violate this.

assumptions_needing_verification.assumption: Universal coefficients K1=0.023, m=-0.125, g_th=35 apply to this propellant
assumptions_needing_verification.coupled_risk: Paper claims +/-10% for 'most practical propellants' but notes negative-erosion outliers. No independent verification for Chunc propellant.

interpretation_labels.source_statement: A claim, equation, range, or fit reported by the cited publication.
interpretation_labels.code_mapping: An algebraic correspondence between published quantities and implementation variables; it does not prove input validity.
interpretation_labels.hypothesis_or_unresolved: An applicability question requiring coupled-input provenance or independent measurement evidence.
